jobs.title: Accounting - Adjunct Faculty
jobs.description: The Student is…. The most important person at MTC Without students, there would be no need for our positions. ….not a cold enrollment statistic, But a flesh and blood human being with feelings and emotions like our own. …not someone to be tolerated so we can do our thing. The student is our thing. POSITION SUMMARY To provide instruction, be accessible as assigned for student conferences (i.e. immediately prior to and following class sessions or by appointment), and maintain adequate and accurate academic performance and attendance records of students – all under the direction of the department dean or representative. ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Respond to inquiries from students, College employees and customers while maintaining standards of confidentiality and privacy, in a timely manner. Maintain confidentiality in accordance with the College, FERPA, student records, and any other protected documentation. Teach approved courses using applied learning methods in accordance with the course objectives, the established syllabus, the schedule of classes, and other College and program requirements. Instruct in a variety of learning environments, both on and off campus, which may include web-based, high schools, and other sites. Demonstrate ability and expertise in one's discipline and enthusiasm and creativity in teaching to create an environment that motivates students to learn. Manage the classroom and maintain records including preparing and updating course syllabi, course materials, technology, and web-based courses. Work with other faculty and the administration in carrying out all instructional procedures and willingness to follow procedures, both at on- and off-campus locations. Maintain accurate records of grades, attendance, etc. and academic performance of students. Maintain accurate records and possess strong organizational skills. Flexibility to meet academic classroom schedules and off-campus sites. Maintain user proficiency for software programs, systems, and databases used by the College. Ability to teach lecture and laboratory courses and operate laboratory equipment. Monitor safety practices within the classroom and laboratory. Attend organizational, orientation, or training meetings held preceding or during each academic term and departmental meetings whenever feasible. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Accounting or other related field; CPA preferred. Exhibit excellent English, communication, and writing skills. Proficiency in Microsoft® Office programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook) with strong computer and related technology skills required. Demonstrate the ability to work independently and complete projects with minimal direction and oversight. Any combination of work experience, training, and/or education equivalent may be accepted. Willingness to work an irregular schedule as assigned. Candidate must successfully pass a background check, prior to and after employment. Valid driver’s license or dependable transportation required. ADA SPECIFICATIONS This position is classified as Faculty and will teach in a wide range of educational venues to provide quality instruction to a diverse student population for the college, primarily in a classroom or office setting. Further information may be obtained from the Office of Human Resources. DISCLAIMER Any other duties deemed appropriate may be assigned - The duties and responsibilities defined above are not an all inclusive list, but a general summary of typical duties. Individuals in this position may be asked to perform a wide range of related tasks, within the scope of their education or certification, to ensure that the highest level of educational services are provided. We all share the responsibility of doing whatever is required to make Marion Technical College a great place to be - for an education and for a career. Adjunct - 3D Modeling
jobs.description: Job Description: The Adjunct – Art, Media, and Design position provides quality instruction and maintains a positive learning environment in the classroom, with major emphasis placed on teaching, supporting and evaluating students. The Adjunct role provides instruction and monitors teaching/learning effectiveness in courses assigned by the Department Chair, or other leadership members. The incumbent must exhibit strong organizational skills and the ability to multitask while engaging large groups of people with complicated material. 3D Modeling Adjuncts will teach courses related to the 3D modeling pipeline using industry standard tools such as Maya, Photoshop, and Unity. They will teach students all aspects of the process including, but not limited to, modeling, cleanup, UV mapping, rigging, animation, and game implementation. The 3D Modeling Adjuncts will stay current with and teach industry best practices and procedures. ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS Instruction & Student Learning Teaches assigned courses as scheduled. Designs curriculum embracing diversity, in all forms, to foster talent in students while modeling inclusive teaching strategies, with an understanding of the socio-cultural issues of traditionally underrepresented groups. Participates in the identification of students with academic or other needs and responds by utilizing an appropriate resource. Uses technology in a manner appropriate to the nature and objectives of courses and programs and communicates clearly to students the expectations concerning the use of such technology. Keeps accurate and appropriate records in accordance with departmental policies. Maintains attendance records, determines and submits grades timely and in accordance with established policies and procedures of the College, and communicates progress feedback, as well as other relevant information to students throughout the semester. Distributes and maintain accurate syllabi that incorporates departmental, college, cross-college, and instructor requirements. Conducts classes punctually and in accordance with the prescribed meeting schedule. Employs appropriate assessment techniques to measure students’ performance in achieving course goals and objectives. Engages in periodic meetings with the department, Lead Instructor, and Chairperson relative to teaching duties and professional development. Student Engagement & Advisement Creates a positive classroom atmosphere that encourages active and collaborative learning, student effort, academic challenge, student and faculty interaction, and support for learners. Uses technology to assist in communication with students. Encourages a sense of community among students for learning both inside and outside the classroom. Refers students to appropriate student and academic support services available at the College or in the community. Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion Helps to ensure the College meets its responsibilities in identifying areas of opportunity and systemic concerns while reporting complaints alleging discrimination. Creates a welcoming, inclusive, equitable and productive work and learning environment where all students, faculty members, and college employees feel valued and are able to contribute to their full potential, regardless of their differences. Ensures accessible and inclusive curriculum design and teaching strategies, and specifically promotes, advises, and supports curriculum development aimed at creating a diverse and equitable learning environment. Fosters and maintains a safe environment of respect and inclusion for faculty, staff, students, and members of the community. Other Duties & Responsibilities: Attend all department meetings and required trainings. Stays current on 3D pipeline software and best practices. We seek a collaborative educator who is excited to contribute to a new academic program and whose teaching and clinical expertise will strengthen the Department's undergraduate curriculum in speech-language pathology. SLCS currently offers an undergraduate program in speech, language, and communication sciences, with a graduate program in speech-language pathology planned to launch in 2031. Consistent with Xavier University's mission, the Department seeks to equip students with the competence and conscience necessary to serve individuals with communication disorders and the professionals and communities who support them. The Department of Speech, Language, and Communication Sciences is part of the College of Health and Human Sciences . CHHS is a leader in experiential learning: 100% of our undergraduate and graduate programs require hands-on learning through field placements, internships, research experiences, and clinical opportunities. In the College of Health and Human Sciences, our commitment to exceptional teaching and mentoring drives us. We focus on scholarship and service in a variety of fields that make a direct and meaningful impact on others. We intentionally strive to create a learning experience that supports all students, incorporates a broad range of perspectives, and fosters an environment of belonging. In alignment with Xavier's Jesuit Catholic mission and Statement of Purpose to “form students who change the world for the better,” we are united across our diverse areas by the shared mission of changing human lives for the better . Many of our College programs, including the Department of Speech, Language, and Communication Sciences, are part of Xavier Health, the University's integrated health initiative connecting a broad portfolio of programs and creating opportunities for collaboration across disciplines. Xavier Health offers more than 15 undergraduate and 12 graduate pathways, more than 500 community partnership sites, and connections across disciplines that contribute to health and human well-being. Xavier Health prepares servant-leaders through real-world experiences and Jesuit Catholic formation that puts the whole person at the center of care. The successful candidate will: Teach undergraduate courses in speech-language pathology, and later, graduate-level curriculum as the Department's graduate program develops toward its planned 2031 launch; Supervise students in clinical and practicum experiences as part of SLCS's experiential learning sequence; Advise and mentor undergraduate (and, in time, graduate) students. Required Qualifications A masters, clinical doctorate, or Ph.D. in Speech-Language Pathology, Communication Sciences and Disorders, or a closely related field. A Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology (CCC-SLP) from the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association (ASHA). Effective written and oral communication skills. A commitment to student advising and mentoring. A commitment to the missions of the Department of Speech, Language, and Communication Sciences and Xavier University, including Xavier's Jesuit Catholic educational tradition. jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty, Data Analytics (Advanced Analytics)
jobs.description: Franklin University, a private, independent, accredited, not-for-profit University located in Columbus, Ohio invites applicants for its Adjunct Faculty, Advanced Analytics position during our Spring 2027 term. The Adjunct Faculty role includes primary responsibility for providing quality instruction and maintaining a positive learning environment with an emphasis placed on teaching, supporting and evaluating students. Position Summary: This post is for a part-time adjunct faculty position to teach a graduate-level course, Advanced Analytics, in an online format (12 weeks). This course examines the data analysis process with the emphasis of quantitative and qualitative findings from data. Students will develop skills in data analytics and predictive analytics that will allow them to develop algorithmic methods and use them along with popular industry software for data-driven solutions. The faculty should develop PowerPoint slides, lesson plans, and demonstrations and should easily be able to provide examples from a number of fields. The faculty should be knowledgeable and experienced with the statistical analysis methods and the use of various analytical tools such as R, and Python, and be able to conduct demonstrations. In addition to the educational qualifications, the candidate should possess excellent communication skills, work ethics, and passion to teach Analytics/Statistics to busy working adult students with flexibility and integrity. Duties and Responsibilities: Teaching a graduate-level analytics/statistics course according to the curriculum, content, and outcomes as specified by the Lead Faculty. The class sessions will be held online. Monitoring and advising students on course-related work, prompt correspondence via email, facilitation of course-related discussions, holding regular office hours and other assigned responsibilities corresponding to the faculty teaching assignment. Timely assessment and evaluation of student assignments including exams, homework assignments, quizzes, projects, discussions, and other activities related to the course. Participation in adjunct MATH/DATA faculty meetings/retreats and associated departmental activities as identified by the Lead Faculty for the assigned course, and responding to Lead Faculty’s requests related to course components. Minimum Requirements/Qualifications: A doctoral degree in Computer Information Systems, Information Systems, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a closely related discipline is required. If the degree is in a related field, at least 18 graduate credit hours should be in the aforementioned fields. At least three years of online teaching experience in higher education. Be skilled in video conferencing platforms Be proficient in online learning management systems Have knowledge and experience with several analytics software such as Tableau, R, and Python. Preferred Skills and Characteristics: A doctoral degree in Engineering, Economics or Business with at least 18 credit hours in the field of Mathematics, Data Science, or Statistics, or doctoral degree in these fields with a graduate certificate in Data Science. At least 5 years of industry experience with specific projects that are targeting the course outcomes. Candidates with experience in data science, data analytics, data visualization, and machine/statistical learning are preferred. jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty, School of Education
jobs.description: Current Xavier University employees must apply to the internal career site by logging into Workday Adjunct Faculty, School of Education ‌ Xavier University is seeking qualified candidates to join our pool of potential adjunct faculty to serve as supervisors of teacher candidates for the 2026-2027 academic year. This posting is intended to collect applications for part-time, non-tenure-track position for an Adjunct Instructor in the School of Education . Candidates must be dedicated to graduate or undergraduate teaching and demonstrate excellence in their field. The successful candidate will contribute to our commitment to excellence in teaching and student engagement. Applications will be accepted on a continuous basis , and candidates may be contacted as teaching needs arise. Adjunct faculty contracts are issued on a semester-by-semester basis , depending on departmental needs and student enrollment. Minimum Qualifications: · Master’s degree in Education or a related field, minimum 5 years K-12 teaching experience, and extensive related experience (e.g., published, leadership, etc.) in the education field or terminal degree in a related field and 5 years K12 teaching experience. · Currently hold and maintain a valid professional educator license. · Flexible availability during the school day is necessary. · University supervisors will need to be proficient with technology such as email, inputting observation notes, fillable PDFs, and other basic computer skills. · University supervisors will serve as a liaison between Xavier University and the field placement, so effective and direct communication skills are necessary. Duties include: · University supervisors will be required to travel to school sites each semester as designated by the Field Coordinator. · Supervisors are expected to observe teacher candidates throughout the semester and provide feedback regarding teacher candidate performance in the areas of dispositions and pedagogy. · Successful supervisors will be able to connect with undergraduate and graduate students to create positive mentorships. · Supervisors will guide, engage and support teacher candidates throughout their development as novice teachers. · Clear and consistent communication with both the teacher candidate and cooperating teacher is required. · Being the first point of contact for both teacher candidate and cooperating, and troubleshooting issues that might arise · Student Teaching Supervision – requires 4-6 site visits · Methods/Clinicals Supervision – requires 1-2 site visits For additional information, please contact Dr. Jody Googins, Co-Director of the School of Education, googinsj@xavier.edu , 513-745-2821. To ensure consideration, interested and qualified applicants must submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae/resume, and the names and contact information of three professional references on Xavier University’s website. Please note: This adjunct faculty pool will close on May 31, 2027 If you are not contacted by this time and remain interested in employment with Xavier University, please reapply to a new adjunct pool posting once it becomes available. Xavier University is an equal opportunity employer. ‌ Benefits - applies only to full-time positions: Xavier University offers a wide array of complementary and affordable benefit options to meet the financial, educational, health, and wellness needs of you and your family. Eligibility varies by position and employment class: Comprehensive insurance plans including medical, dental, vision and prescription coverage. Tax advantaged accounts including health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts, and dependent care account. Financial security via life and long-term disability insurance, accident and illness insurance, and retirement savings plans. Generous paid time off work options including vacation, sick leave and holidays. Tuition remission for employees and their eligible dependents.

jobs.title: Adjunct Instructor in Education: K-5 Mathematics Methods
jobs.description: Adjunct Instructor in Education: K-5 Mathematics Methods The following statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. POSITION SUMMARY: Bluffton University Department of Education is seeking an experienced and student-centered Adjunct Faculty member to teach K–5 Mathematics Methods courses within the Educator Preparation Program. The successful candidate will bring expertise in elementary mathematics instruction and a demonstrated commitment to preparing future educators to teach mathematics effectively, confidently, and equitably. The instructor will provide preservice teachers with research-based instructional strategies, practical classroom applications, and opportunities to develop the knowledge and skills necessary to plan, implement, assess, and differentiate high-quality mathematics instruction for students in grades K–5. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Teach an undergraduate K–5 Mathematics Methods course in accordance with college and program standards. Prepare and deliver engaging, evidence-based instruction focused on effective mathematics teaching practices for elementary learners. Model instructional strategies and pedagogical approaches appropriate for students in grades K–5. Guide teacher candidates in developing mathematics lesson plans, learning activities, assessments, and instructional sequences aligned with state and national mathematics standards. Support teacher candidates in understanding mathematical concepts, student mathematical thinking, and common misconceptions. Address differentiated instruction and strategies for meeting the needs of diverse learners, including students with varying levels of mathematical readiness. Integrate problem solving, mathematical reasoning, discourse, representation, fluency, and conceptual understanding into methods instruction. Incorporate appropriate technology, manipulatives, and other instructional resources to support elementary mathematics learning. Provide timely, constructive feedback on assignments, lesson plans, and other course-related work. Maintain accurate course records and comply with college policies, procedures, and academic expectations. Collaborate with education faculty and contribute to the continued development of the teacher preparation program as appropriate. QUALIFICATIONS: Minimum: Master’s degree in Education or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Five or more years of successful teaching experience in mathematics at the K–5 level. Demonstrated knowledge of effective elementary mathematics pedagogy and instructional practices. Strong understanding of elementary mathematics content and the developmental needs of K–5 learners. Experience designing and implementing standards-aligned mathematics instruction and assessment. Excellent communication, organization, and interpersonal skills Preferred: Experience teaching mathematics methods or supervising preservice teachers in a teacher preparation program. Experience working with adult learners, teacher candidates, or professional development programs. Knowledge of current research and best practices in elementary mathematics education. Familiarity with state and national mathematics standards, including the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics. Experience integrating educational technology into mathematics instruction. Current or prior elementary teaching licensure/certification. Physical Demands/Work Environment: The position includes approximately twelve hours of in-person classes and labs per week plus attendance at meetings and other events on campus each week. Lab work includes some physical labor demands. Some occasional travel off campus may be needed for conferences and/or off campus meetings. Employment decisions are based on merit and university needs, and not on race, color

jobs.description: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing program at Baldwin Wallace University invites applications for part-time adjunct faculty members from nurses with teaching experience at either the collegiate level or in a hospital setting. Responsibilities: The following outlines the essential functions of the position and is not to be considered a detailed description of all duties inherent in the position . Provide direct supervision of students in the clinical setting and lab settings. Prepare students to think critically, communicate accurately, and perform indicated therapeutic nursing interventions in assigned patient care situations. Collaborate with the director of clinical education in structuring clinical assignments to assist students in the application of theoretical learning to clinical patient situations. Evaluate student performance and provide feedback to enhance student learning. Participate in nursing faculty meetings and department/university events. Required (Minimum) Qualifications: At least two years of experience as a registered nurse, Evidence of clinical competency in Medical-Surgical or specialty (pediatric, obstetric, behavioral health) nursing, A current, valid, unencumbered license as a registered nurse in the state of Ohio, Clean background check and drug screen (to be done after interview), and Earned nursing degree: Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) -- required if the basic nursing degree is not a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN). Applicants with a BSN must be currently enrolled in a program leading to a master’s or doctoral degree. Preferred Qualifications: Earned MSN degree with a specialization in Nursing Education or coursework in instruction, curriculum development and/or student evaluation. Professional experience in a behavioral health setting. Earned PhD or DNP degree. Nursing scholarship or research experience. Baldwin Wallace University is a private liberal arts college located 14 miles southwest of Cleveland. Total enrollment is approximately 4,400 with 3,200 full-time undergraduate day students. Baldwin Wallace’s close proximity to the cultural benefits of Cleveland provides countless educational and entertainment opportunities for student and faculty members. In a continuing effort to enrich its academic environment and provide equal educational and employment opportunities, the University actively encourages applications from individuals who desire an environment celebrating diversity. How to Apply: Review of complete applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. For the strongest consideration, applicants should submit materials by May 12, 2025. Please submit the following materials, assembled into one (1) Word document or PDF attachment at the time of application. Once an application is submitted, applicants will not be able to edit attachments. A letter of application Curriculum vitae or resume Statement of teaching philosophy Names and contact information for three current professional references BW’s Employment and Careers’ web page may be accessed at https://www.bw.edu/employment Baldwin Wallace University is an EEO employer and educator. We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. At BW, we support and encourage diversity in a variety of forms. We value and appreciate inclusive excellence in the classroom, within extracurricular activities and as we engage our community partners.

Demonstrate ability and expertise in one's discipline and enthusiasm and creativity in teaching to create an environment that motivates students to learn. jobs.title: Aspire Instructor
jobs.description: The Student is…. The most important person at MTC Without students, there would be no need for our positions. ….not a cold enrollment statistic, But a flesh and blood human being with feelings and emotions like our own. …not someone to be tolerated so we can do our thing. The student is our thing. POSITION SUMMARY Provide quality teaching and learning, diagnostics, assessment, advise students, and complete other assignments that enable the department to achieve its purpose and advance the mission of Marion Technical College (the “College”). ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES, FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1) Maintain confidentiality and privacy in accordance with the College, FERPA, student records, and any other protected documentation. 2) Provide quality teaching in assigned Aspire courses to meet objectives and student learning needs corresponding to the level and content of each course and to Ohio’s Aspire standards. 3) Demonstrate expertise, enthusiasm, and creativity in teaching; produce an environment where learning and self-improvement occur. 4) Communicate effectively, facilitate the learning process by utilizing appropriate methods, and prepare and update assigned individual lesson plans on a regular basis. 5) Demonstrate knowledge of instructional methods, developmental education, student success strategies, curriculum development principles, diverse learning styles, and best practices in helping at-risk students succeed. 6) Proficient with technology and willing to learn and apply distance education techniques. 7) Work collaboratively with all student support service areas throughout the college that focus on at-risk students, including admissions, tutoring, mentoring, and first-year advisors. 8) Conduct and assist with student orientation and follow-up. Direct and provide tutorial assistance to students. 9) Meet with the Director and other teachers from Aspire sites. Maintain classroom and other records. 10) Participate effectively as a team member, demonstrating group problem solving/decision-making ability with good communication skills and the ability to relate well with co-workers, student, and community members. 11) Attend a minimum of two professional development activities per year. 12) Supervise and provide direction to aids and/or volunteers. Build and maintain relationships with students, participants, the College, and community members. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This position is grant-funded and contingent upon the continuation of external funding. This position may be eliminated or reduced with or without notice, if funding should cease or be reduced. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree from a regionally-accredited college or university in Education or related field required; Master's degree from a regionally-accredited college or university preferred. Prior teaching experience in an Aspire program or at a college or university preferred. Willingness to work an irregular schedule as assigned. Ability to successfully pass a background check, prior to and after employment. Valid driver’s license or dependable transportation required. ADA SPECIFICATIONS This position is classified as Faculty and will teach in a wide range of educational venues to provide quality instruction to a diverse student population for the college, primarily in a classroom or office setting. Further information may be obtained from Human Resources. DISCLAIMER Any other duties deemed appropriate may be assigned - The duties and responsibilities defined above are not an all-inclusive list, but a general summary of typical duties. Individuals in this position may be asked to perform a wide range of related tasks, within the scope of their education or certification, to ensure that the highest level of educational services are provided. We all share the responsibility of doing whatever is required to make Marion Technical College a great place to be - for an education and for a career.

jobs.title: Assistant / Associate / Professor of Voice
jobs.description: Job Summary The Cleveland Institute of Music (CIM) invites applications from nationally or internationally recognized artist-teachers for a full-time faculty appointment in Voice (Tenor, Baritone, Bass-Baritone, or Bass). While this position will begin with the 2027-28 academic year, CIM seeks to fill it in time to include the successful candidate in the audition process, starting in early 2027. In alignment with CIM’s mission, vision, and institutional learning goals , the successful candidate will teach assigned applied voice students, primarily in the Conservatory, but their studio may also include occasional students from the Academy (pre-college) or cross-registered students from Case Western Reserve University. Ideal candidates will demonstrate a proven record of recruiting and teaching outstanding students in a conservatory or university music school, experience guiding students along multiple stages of development, and a noted reputation as a performer. Review of applications begins September 28, 2026 [FG4] , and continues until the position is filled. Please submit a cover letter that responds to CIM’s mission and vision; statement of your teaching philosophy; CV; links to 2-3 videos of solo, opera or concert performances; and 3-5 references with contact information. Additional materials may be requested at a later date. This is a bargaining unit position covered by the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) between CIM and AFM Local 4. The hired individual will be ranked as Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor depending on qualifications. CIM and the hired individual will negotiate compensation and a personal contract, within the pay ranges of the CBA and subject to its terms and conditions of employment. [FG5] Primary Duties and Responsibilities Empower each student to perform with technical prowess and informed, compelling artistry in pursuit of a top echelon music career or, for Academy students, in pursuit of study at a top collegiate program, by: Comprehensively and sequentially guiding them through their course of applied study during their degree or program at CIM. Teaching applied voice lessons and studio classes. Preparing students for regular participation in performances. Preparing students for curricular assessment requirements. Mentoring students along their educational and career paths. Maintain national/international visibility, actively recruit prospective students, and participate in all stages of the application, audition, and enrollment process. Serve on faculty panels for hearings, juries, recitals, etc. Depending on background and experience, responsibilities may include teaching repertoire, pedagogy, diction, or opera training classes; directing or assisting with opera scenes; coaching vocal chamber ensembles; and other related instructional activities. Communicate promptly, professionally, and effectively with students, families, faculty, and administration. Adhere to Faculty Duties and Expectations document and Employee Handbook. Education, Experience and Qualifications A qualified candidate will possess: A Doctor of Musical Arts degree in voice or a master’s degree in voice with demonstrated relevant experience or must meet CIM’s Tested Equivalency Policy. A minimum of 5 years of experience teaching promising students of various ages and levels, and a track record of helping them achieve their desired outcomes. A reputation as a successful solo, opera, and/or concert performer. An awareness of various pedagogical approaches and the ability to apply them to each student’s unique needs and goals. An extensive knowledge of a diverse and dynamic repertoire that can inspire and connect with students and audiences from a variety of backgrounds. Personal Attributes The ideal candidate is an excellent musician and focused teacher whose experiences and passions are oriented towards guiding, developing, and nurturing students. This role requires: Curiosity

jobs.description: Employment Opportunities Assistant Clinical Professor - Clinical Mental Health Counseling Apply now Job No: 503899 Work Type: Faculty Full Time Location: Dayton, OH Category: Faculty Department: Counselor Education - 210400 Advertised: September 22, 2026 Applications close: October 01, 2026 Position Summary: Are you looking for a faculty position where you can:Engage in the holistic development of future Clinical Mental Health Counselors,Work in an integrative, collaborative, interdisciplinary environment,Mentor and teach highly motivated students,Be part of a mission-driven institution,Live affordably in a central location with easy access to both recreation & urban amenities?The University of Dayton provides this opportunity! The University of Dayton Department of Counselor Education and Human Services is seeking applications for a full-time, 12-month, Assistant Clinical Faculty specializing in Clinical Mental Health Counseling beginning January 1, 2027. Clinical Mental Health Counseling faculty teach in a CACREP-accredited M.S.Ed. program. The OpportunityThe University of Dayton’s Clinical Mental Health Counseling program offers opportunities for faculty engagement and growth through teaching; interprofessional collaboration; and curriculum, program, and community outreach development. We have an established partnership with two other universities for Interprofessional Education and Practice (IPE) which prepares students in health professions to work well together. Our faculty work collaboratively with students and community partners to extend learning beyond the classroom through such programs as the Community Wellness Initiative, Brain Health Collective, Ecotherapy Certificate program, and Chi Sigma Iota. As a member of this dynamic team, this position is expected to: Teach graduate counseling courses on our Dayton and Columbus campuses (12 credits per term; fall, spring, & summer); Work primarily from our main campus in Dayton, OH with one evening per week of teaching in Columbus (mileage provided); Serve as Clinical Experience Coordinator (including but not limited to: site development, overseeing student placements, supervisor training, & clinical documentation); Recruit, advise, and mentor graduate students; Serve as co-faculty advisor for Chi Sigma Iota chapters; Provide service to the program, department, university, community, and profession; and Demonstrate a commitment to inclusive excellence. Salary is competitive and dependent upon qualifications. Summer teaching is a requirement of this 12-month position. Research is not required for this position but is supported. UD’s School of Education and Health Sciences offers a pathway for promotion for clinical faculty. The Program and DepartmentThe University of Dayton’s Clinical Mental Health Counseling Program is a well-established master’s program with campuses in both Dayton and Columbus. Students from UD’s CMHC program complete clinical training with a wide variety of community partners (e.g. community mental health agencies, hospitals, university counseling centers, nursing homes, school-based organizations, etc). Students also engage with faculty in research, community outreach, interprofessional development, and skill specialization through our Ecotherapy Certificate program, Ecotherapy Club, and Community Wellness Initiative. This position combines opportunities for teaching, overseeing practicum and internship, community engagement, developing programs, interprofessional collaboration, and engaging students in community outreach. jobs.description: Job Title Assistant or Associate Professor - Information Systems Department Information Systems and Analytics Department Worker Type Regular Pay Type Salary Salary will be commensurate with the level of the position, education, and experience. Benefit Eligible Yes Screening Date 2026-09-01 Job Description Summary Miami University invites applications for the position of Assistant or Associate Professor of Information Systems to teach technical and/or managerial courses in information systems starting Fall 2027. Current department faculty members will be talking to interested candidates at AMCIS. Job Description The successful candidate will teach courses in the Information Systems & Cybersecurity Management (ISCM) program, maintain an active research agenda that results in publications in top-tier information systems journals; contribute to the growth of the Information Systems and Cybersecurity Management (ISCM) program; advise students; provide service to the institution and profession; and engage with the business community. The Information Systems & Analytics (ISA) department at Miami University offers academic programs that integrate the fields of Information Systems, Business Analytics, Cybersecurity Management, and Artificial Intelligence for Business. Our mission is to empower students with the knowledge and skills to derive insights from data, use emerging technologies to advance business objectives, and address emerging cybersecurity challenges. Our department is composed of approximately 22 dedicated faculty members who foster a strong culture of collaboration within the Farmer School of Business, across Miami University, and with industry partners. Our rigorous academic programs focus on real-world data, experiential learning, and a project-based curriculum. The ISA Department offers a major in ISCM with separate tracks in Information Systems and Cybersecurity Management. Additionally, we offer a Master of Science in Business Analytics, a major in Business Analytics and several minors, including Business Analytics, Information Systems, Cybersecurity Management, and Artificial Intelligence for Business. We also offer a certificate in Artificial Intelligence for Business and Cybersecurity Management. Minimum Requirements: Required: Doctorate in information systems or a closely related field by the date of appointment (or must be completed by December 31, 2027, for appointment to a second year), with prior experience in teaching information systems courses in a business school environment for appointment as an Assistant Professor. For appointment as an Associate Professor, applicants must also demonstrate excellence in research, with publications in high-quality journals in information systems and a strong teaching portfolio in information systems. Consideration will be given to candidates with previous research success and/or a promising research pipeline in information systems; relevant work and leadership experience to advance our Information Systems & Cybersecurity Management program, and its alignment with emerging digital and AI-driven business practices. Additional Position Information (if applicable) Required Application Documents Cover letter, curriculum vitae, evidence of teaching effectiveness through recent teaching evaluations, teaching philosophy, research statement, and graduate transcripts. Benefit Eligible Yes Screening Date 2026-10-12 Job Description Summary The Department of Psychology at Miami University invites applications for an Assistant Professor (tenure-track) position in Cognitive Neuroscience to begin Fall 2027. Candidate should have a strong research and publication record; a strong commitment to both graduate and undergraduate training; and the ability to teach graduate and undergraduate courses in cognition/neuroscience, advise graduate and undergraduate students, and perform university and professional service. Job Description Engagement in both research and innovative teaching are highly valued in our department and university. Research interests should focus on examining neural mechanisms that underlie cognition and behavior, with particular interest in candidates whose work addresses health-related questions, including mental or neurological health, aging, stress, disease, health behaviors, or other factors influencing brain and behavioral functioning. The School Psychology Program is NASP-approved and CAEP accredited, and offers an M.S. and Ed.S. degree in school psychology. Benefit Eligible Yes Screening Date 2026-08-01 Job Description Summary The Department of Entrepreneurship in the Farmer School of Business at Miami University invite applications for an Assistant Professor in Entrepreneurship (tenure track) to teach courses in entrepreneurship; maintain an active research program and publish in highly regarded management and entrepreneurship journals; advise students; and provide service to the department, division and University. Appointment begins Fall 2027. Job Description We seek an active scholar and passionate educator to publish in top-tier management and entrepreneurship journals, teach high-impact undergraduate courses, mentor students, and contribute to our vibrant campus and regional entrepreneurial ecosystem. The Department of Entrepreneurship combines top-tier academic scholarship and rigorous empirical research with practice-based learning across several core pillars: startup and venture capital, social entrepreneurship and impact investing, corporate innovation, technology commercialization, and entrepreneurial mindset. Distinguishing Features: Scholarly Excellence: Our faculty regularly publish in premier management and entrepreneurship journals, including AMJ, AMR, SMJ, SEJ, Strategy Science, JBV, ETP, JOM, JBE, and Organization Science . Experiential Focus: High touch, personalized learning delivered by teacher-scholars with founder experience, and practice-based learning embedded in every course and co-curricular program. Broad Impact: Interdisciplinary curriculum engaging students from every undergraduate major across campus, integrated deeply with local and national ecosystem builders. For more information, please visit the Department of Entrepreneurship Webpage . Minimum Qualifications: Required: Ph.D. in Entrepreneurship or a closely related field by date of appointment for appointment as Assistant Professor. ABDs may apply, but all degree requirements must be completed by the date of appointment (doctorate must be awarded by December 31, 2027, for appointment to the second year). Demonstrated commitment to instructional excellence and evidence of high-quality undergraduate teaching effectiveness. Research Interests & Streams: We welcome scholars across various research streams in entrepreneurship and innovation. Consideration will be given to candidates with established research record in one of the following areas: Social or environmental issues in entrepreneurship. The impact of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies on venture creation. Entrepreneurial finance. Entrepreneurial ecosystems, economic development, or hybrid organizations. Consideration will be given to candidates with a promising research pipeline targeted at leading management and entrepreneurship journals, backed by a strong foundation in empirical research (quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods). jobs.description: Job Title Assistant Professor - Quantum Information Science and Technology (Experiment) Department Physics Department Worker Type Regular Pay Type Salary Salary will be commensurate with the level of the position, education, and experience. Benefit Eligible Yes Screening Date 2026-10-15 Job Description Summary The Department of Physics is hiring a tenure-track Assistant Professor in experimental Quantum Information Science and Technology starting in August 2027. The selected candidate will build an externally funded research program, teach undergraduate and graduate physics courses, mentor students at all levels, and contribute to institutional service. This role is part of a major university-wide expansion in quantum initiatives that includes a new quantum institute, new degree programs, and cluster hires. The successful candidate will expand the department's existing quantum research capabilities while opening new avenues for interdisciplinary collaboration. Job Description The Department of Physics seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor in experimental Quantum Information Science and Technology (QIST) beginning August 2027 to develop a nationally-recognized externally-funded research program; to teach undergraduate and graduate level courses in physics; and to provide service to the institution. Candidates with expertise in quantum sensing and metrology are preferred. Current faculty research in QIST includes quantum optics, cold atom physics, molecular spectroscopy, topologically-protected magnetic materials, and quantum information theory. Job Description The Behavioral and Justice Sciences Program in the College of Business and Humanities at the University of Findlay invites applications for a full-time, non-tenure track position in Criminal Justice/Pre-Law beginning in August 2026. The Behavioral and Justice Sciences Program is seeking a dynamic and knowledgeable instructor to teach both lower and upper level undergraduate courses in both criminal justice and law. The ideal candidate will contribute to our mission of delivering a student-centered education and fostering an environment of pedagogical excellence, experiential learning, professional development, service, and scholarship. This position is an exciting opportunity to join a dedicated team of educators who are devoted to preparing students for meaningful lives and productive careers. Key Responsibilities: Teach lower and upper-level criminal justice and law courses in both seated and online formats. Develop and deliver engaging course materials that meet the department's academic standards. Develop and deliver experiential learning activities to students promoting active learning and professional development. Advise and provide mentorship to undergraduate students. Collaborate with faculty and staff to enhance student learning and meet departmental strategic objectives. Assist the Behavioral and Justice Sciences Department with program marketing, student recruitment, assessment activities, and other initiatives as directed by the department chair, director, dean, and university administration Engage in professional development activities and scholarship to stay current in the field of criminal justice. Qualifications: The requirement for this position is a JD degree from an ABA accredited program who is a member of the state bar association with tested experience in practicing law. Those with a Ph.D. in law or a Ph.D. in criminal justice with an emphasis in law will also be considered. Preference will be given to those who have tested experience in criminal law and the criminal justice profession. Candidates should possess the ability to work effectively and collegially with a diverse group of students, faculty, administrators, and staff. Candidates should demonstrate strong passion/commitment to teaching excellence, student advising and mentorship, experiential learning, professional development, university/community service, and scholarship. Candidates must have the ability to develop and deliver curriculum, meet the demands of the position in a timely manner, and assess student learning outcomes. Moreover, candidates should have outstanding communication and interpersonal skills and the potential to assume leadership roles within the college. The University of Findlay is a comprehensive master's institution and the largest private university in northwest Ohio with more than 3,600 students enrolled in diverse academic programs. Teaching excellence is the top priority of the University faculty. jobs.description: Assistant Professor of Environmental Studies and Biology, Tenure-track 493346 Gambier, OH, Ohio Biology Faculty View favorites Kenyon College invites applications for a tenure-track position in the Departments of Environmental Studies and Biology (Freshwater Ecosystem or Landscape Ecology) starting in July 2027. We seek a broadly trained ecologist with expertise in freshwater ecosystem or landscape ecology, with an interest in contributing to an interdisciplinary department. To complement current faculty expertise, we seek candidates whose research focuses on regional or global ecological or biogeochemical processes, preferably in freshwater systems. Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to excellent teaching, including strong academic support, inclusive course experiences, and effective mentoring for our diverse student population. Teaching expectations are 5 courses per year, with 3 courses in the Environmental Studies Department (e.g., Introduction to Environmental Studies, Senior Seminar in Environmental Studies, and new lecture and/or lab courses at the upper level) and 2 courses in the Biology Department (e.g., Introductory Biology lecture or lab, Aquatic Systems Biology). Additional opportunities exist for interdisciplinary teaching and scholarship within and outside the sciences, including in Kenyon's interdisciplinary Program in Computing and the college's Science and Nature Writing initiative. We expect a vigorous research program that involves undergraduate students, leads to publications, and has potential to attract extramural funding. Applicants should hold a Ph.D degree; post-doctoral experience is preferred. We encourage applications from all groups historically underrepresented in the sciences. A complete application will be composed of 1) a cover letter (maximum 2 pages); 2) a Curriculum Vitae (no page limit); 3) a statement of the applicant's teaching philosophy that addresses the applicant’s experiences and plans for teaching a diverse student body (maximum 2 pages); 4) a statement of the applicant’s research and scholarship that includes plans for collaborative research with undergraduates (maximum 3 pages); 5) an unofficial graduate transcript; and 6) contact information for three professional references. All application materials must be submitted electronically through Kenyon's employment website: http://careers.kenyon.edu. Review of applications will begin on August 31, 2026. Please direct questions to Natalie Wright, Search Committee Chair (wright1@kenyon.edu). Kenyon College is a nationally prominent, private liberal arts college where academic excellence goes hand in hand with a strong sense of community and close relationships among students and professors. Situated along the beautiful Kokosing River, with a 700-acre nature preserve, Kenyon is an ideal place to study and teach ecology. Kenyon has an established record of preparing students for graduate study and research careers, ranking 8th nationally in the proportion of STEM graduates who go on to earn doctoral degrees. Our students regularly earn nationally competitive awards, including Fulbright Fellowships and National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program awards. Compensation and Benefits Salaries at Kenyon are competitive and are commensurate with experience. There are a number of faculty development opportunities (e.g. travel, research funds, etc.) for which appointees are eligible. In addition to an attractive salary, Kenyon offers benefits for employees and their family members. Children of employees are eligible for 100% tuition waivers at Kenyon, and through the Great Lakes Colleges Association, children of employees are eligible for 85% tuition waivers at fifteen other of the nation's finest liberal arts colleges. We also offer health and dental insurance, TIAA retirement, and many other benefits, including provisions for a spouse, families, and domestic partners. jobs.description: Career Opportunities at Ohio Northern University Job Summary: Ohio Northern University's Pettit College of Law seeks candidates for three full-time, entry-level faculty positions on the tenure track. The College of Law has interest in a variety of teaching areas, including but not limited to Contracts, Sales, Secured Transactions, Property, Criminal Law, Criminal Procedure, and Evidence, and qualified lateral candidates will also be considered. ONU Law is a closely knit community focused on preparing practice-ready lawyers, with an Advocacy program ranked among the best in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. Job Description : Ohio Northern University's Pettit College of Law seeks candidates for three full-time, entry-level faculty positions on the tenure track. The College of Law has interest in a variety of teaching areas, including but not limited to Contracts, Sales, Secured Transactions, Property, Criminal Law, Criminal Procedure, and Evidence. Qualified lateral candidates will also be considered. Ohio Northern is a private university affiliated with the United Methodist Church, and its Pettit College of Law is a closely knit community built around small classes and individualized faculty mentoring. For more than 140 years, ONU Law has focused its educational mission on preparing practice-ready lawyers, an emphasis reflected in our clinical and externship placements and an Advocacy program ranked among the best in the nation by U.S. News & World Report. ONU Law is also home to one of the nation's first fully online part-time JD program accredited by the ABA. Candidates with experience as a practicing lawyer, judicial clerk, or law teacher are preferred, and we welcome candidates who bring a range of teaching interests and approaches, including experience with varied instructional formats and delivery methods. Expectations include a normal teaching load of four courses per year, scholarly research and publication, and service obligations for the 2027-2028 academic year. Candidates must have a J.D. from a law school accredited by the A.B.A. or an equivalent degree from a foreign institution, a distinguished academic record, and a commitment to excellence in teaching and scholarship. Ohio Northern University was founded in 1871, and ONU Law has been educating lawyers since 1885. Ohio Northern is located in Ada, Ohio, a quiet college community known for its small-town charm, about an hour from the growing Columbus metro area, and is home to five colleges and about 3,140 students representing 50 states and 15 countries. Ohio Northern University offers a competitive salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and skills. Fringe benefits include the TIAA-CREF retirement program, medical insurance, disability benefits, life insurance, tuition remission for dependents attending Ohio Northern University for an initial baccalaureate degree, and eligibility for participation in The Tuition Exchange, a program involving over 640 member colleges and universities. Interested candidates are strongly encouraged to apply quickly to ensure immediate review. Posting Details Announcement Information Job Summary The Conservatory of Music at Oberlin College invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the level of Assistant Professor in Music Theory and Aural Skills, beginning with the 2027-2028 academic year. The Division of Music Theory is especially interested in qualified candidates who can contribute through their teaching, research, and/or service to the diversity and excellence of our academic and musical community. We encourage applications from candidates who will bring a fresh perspective to our existing courses and whose expertise encompasses a broad range of repertoires and methodologies. We also encourage applications from previous applicants. About The Oberlin Conservatory of Music, founded in 1865, is the nation’s oldest continuously operating conservatory, and the only major music school in the country linked with a preeminent liberal arts college. Students are enrolled in undergraduate programs leading to the Bachelor of Music in performance, jazz studies, composition, technology in music and related arts, recording arts and production, music theater, and musicology. Oberlin also offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Music in conducting, the Master of Music in performance on historical instruments, the Master of Fine Arts in piano technology, and artist diplomas. Oberlin’s Music Theory Division consists of eleven tenured and tenure-track faculty members with a shared commitment to innovative pedagogy and research excellence. We serve over 600 conservatory and college students per semester in core theory, core aural skills, upper division seminars, and courses directed to majors and non-majors from the college of arts and sciences. Our students are creative, musical, and engaged. We have recently reconceived our theory curriculum, which now consists of a first-year core embracing topics including rhythm and meter, melody and counterpoint, harmony, form, and texture and timbre, and which creates space for engagement with music from a variety of perspectives. The second-year curriculum consists of elective courses determined by faculty interest; upcoming offerings include “Analyzing American Musicals,” “Cycles,” “East Asia in Western Art Music,” “Large Forms,” “Music in Time,” “Polyphonies,” “Questioning Genius,” “Scales, Sets, Series, and Spectra,” “Theory and Analysis of Post-2000 Pop Music,” and “Writing in Tonal Style.” The division’s pedagogical ethos is collaborative; new hires will be given materials and guidance to help them prepare for the first-year core but will also have freedom to adapt the course content to suit their own pedagogical and intellectual interests.Candidates are encouraged to think creatively about potential second-year elective courses they would like to offer and describe them in their cover letter. Oberlin provides resources of both time and money in support of faculty research. Faculty are eligible to apply for grants to fund research expenses and are entitled to a pre-tenure sabbatical

Top candidates will expand and complement the existing strengths of the microbiology and immunology faculty. Candidates are expected to contribute to the training and teaching of professional, postgraduate, and graduate learners, as well as provide institutional service. Candidates will join a highly-collaborative, multidisciplinary research community, and will be provided with newly renovated laboratory space along with generous start-up funds and competitive compensation packages. jobs.description: Job Title Assistant/Associate Professor - CPB Department Chemical, Paper and Biomedical Engineering Department Worker Type Regular Pay Type Salary Salary will be commensurate with the level of the position, education, and experience. Benefit Eligible Yes Screening Date 2026-10-01 Job Description Summary Assistant/Associate Professor (tenure track) to teach courses in biomedical engineering and related areas, develop an active externally funded research program in biomedical engineering, advise undergraduate and graduate students, and provide service to the department, university, and profession. Candidates with expertise in all areas of biomedical engineering are welcome, but preference will be given to candidates with expertise in the fields of biomechanics, biomaterials, and medical device design. Proposed research programs focusing on aging, AI-utilization, and other emerging techniques will be given priority. Appointment begins August, 2027. Job Description The Department of Chemical, Paper and Biomedical Engineering (CPB) at Miami University offers a collaborative interdisciplinary environment that fosters cutting-edge research and innovation. With a commitment to excellence in education, the department provides well-equipped laboratory facilities, access to diverse research initiatives, and a collaborative culture that integrates engineering principles with biomedical advancements. The department is strengthening and expanding its research portfolio in biomedical engineering and is looking to fill a gap in biomechanics, but also desires to expand research in biomaterials and medical device design. Demonstrated research experience focused on aging-related application, AI utilization, or incorporating other cutting-edge methodology is important for this position. CPB Faculty have access to several core facilities on campus including the Center for Advanced Microscopy and Imaging (CAMI), the Center for Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics, the Miami University Instrumentation Laboratory, the Miami University NMR/MS Facility, and the the RedHawk Computing Cluster. Miami University is known for its emphasis on teaching excellence, with strong support for innovative pedagogy and mentorship. Located in Oxford, Ohio, the campus offers a dynamic academic community within a beautiful and welcoming environment. Candidates will find the department an ideal place to launch and grow impactful research programs while contributing to the training of future leaders in biomedical engineering. jobs.description: About Walsh University Walsh University is seeking a dynamic, energetic, and passionate individual who is enthusiastic about contributing to a private, faithfully Catholic institution of higher learning and serving the common good. Walsh University promotes academic excellence, an engaged community, and a commitment to helping students discover their life purpose. Grounded in values of faith, excellence, integrity, service, and community, Walsh University is committed to principles of equal opportunity and is an equal opportunity employer. About the Program Exercise Science is a division within the College of Health Sciences. The division includes both a growing undergraduate Exercise Science program delivered in a traditional face-to-face format and an online Master of Exercise Physiology program. Both programs are accredited by the American Society of Exercise Physiologists (ASEP). The division is currently staffed by three full-time faculty members holding doctoral degrees in Exercise Physiology who primarily support the instructional responsibilities of both the undergraduate and graduate programs. Faculty are encouraged to pursue collaborative scholarship and interdisciplinary engagement across the College of Health Sciences. The Bachelor of Science degree in Exercise Science is offered through five curriculum tracks designed to prepare students for a variety of professional and graduate education pathways. While all Exercise Science majors complete a common core curriculum, students may pursue specialized tracks in: Pre-Physical Therapy Pre-Occupational Therapy Pre-Athletic Training Pre-Physician Assistant Studies Applied Exercise Science (Professional ) In addition to the undergraduate curriculum, high-achieving students may pursue accelerated pathways into Walsh University’s graduate programs in Physical Therapy and Occupational Therapy, as well as Athletic Training at Youngstown State University through an established articulation agreement. The successful candidate will demonstrate a broad understanding of exercise science and the ability to teach across the undergraduate curriculum in both face-to-face and online formats, with potential opportunities for graduate-level instruction. This position supports the University’s mission of educating students in the Catholic intellectual tradition while preparing graduates for professional practice, advanced study, and leadership in health and human performance fields. jobs.description: Job Title Assistant/Associate Teaching Professor or Associate Lecturer - Paper Science and Engineering Department Chemical, Paper and Biomedical Engineering Department Worker Type Regular Pay Type Salary Salary will be commensurate with the level of the position, education, and experience. Benefit Eligible Yes Screening Date 2026-10-01 Job Description Summary Seeking individuals to teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in Paper Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, and related topics; mentor students; provide service to the institution. The start date is August 2027. Job Description The Department of Chemical, Paper and Biomedical Engineering invites applications for a position at the rank of Assistant/Associate Teaching Professor or Associate Lecturer . The focus of this search is to find candidates with educational and/or work experience directly related to the pulp and paper industry. Successful candidates will be expected to teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in Paper Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering, and related topics, mentor students, and contribute service to the department and university. The typical teaching load for this position is 24 semester credit hours per year, with approximately 80% of the workload dedicated to teaching and approximately 20% devoted to service. This position will begin in August 2027. Based on performance, this position is eligible for subsequent reappointment with the possibility of promotion tiers that includes longer-term continuing contracts. The Department of Chemical, Paper and Biomedical Engineering is the oldest engineering program on campus. Pulp and paper-related courses were first offered in 1958 at Miami. With the help of industry and alumni, the Paper Science and Engineering Foundation was established in 1960. The mission of the Foundation is to support the department in attracting and preparing talented and highly motivated individuals for careers in leadership within the pulp, paper, and affiliated industries. This is accomplished by providing scholarships and work experience opportunities to students, support to faculty, enhancements to department facilities, and by demonstrating the value of the program to the industry. The Paper Science and Engineering program became the first ABET-accredited Paper Science and Engineering program in the United States in 1999. Miami University is known for its emphasis on teaching excellence, with strong support for innovative pedagogy and mentorship. Located in Oxford, Ohio, the campus offers a dynamic academic community within a beautiful and welcoming environment. Candidates will find the department an ideal place to launch and grow impactful research programs while contributing to the training of future leaders in the paper industry. ( https://miamioh.edu/cec/departments/chemical-paper-biomedical-engineering/ ) Minimum Qualifications: Required: For appointment as an Assistant Teaching Professor , applicants must have a doctorate in Paper Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Engineering Education, or related field by the date of appointment. jobs.description: Employment Opportunities Associate Professor & Mary Ann Spearin Chair in Catholic Theology Apply now Job No: 503904 Work Type: Faculty Full Time Location: Dayton, OH Category: Faculty Department: Religious Studies - 208490 Advertised: September 22, 2026 Applications close: November 01, 2026 Position Summary: The Opportunity The Department of Theology and Religious Studies at the University of Dayton seeks applications for the Mary Ann Spearin Chair in Catholic Theology. This endowed chair, established by Mary Ann Spearin to support graduate theological education at the University of Dayton, is open at the rank of associate professor in the Department of Theology and Religious Studies. This is a nine month, tenured faculty position with an appointment to the Spearin Chair that is made for a renewable four-year term, beginning August 16, 2027. We seek a strong and creative scholar who can steward our programs’ successes going forward. Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate experience in administration, teaching, and scholarship, with attention to the specific and unique foci of our graduate programs. Key Responsibilities Teaching theology courses in the MA and PhD programs, including regular teaching of one of the required PhD seminars; teach undergraduate courses at the discretion of, and in conversation with, the department chairperson. The typical teaching load per year for this position is 2-1. Contributing scholarship that advances their particular field of study and that connects broadly to the doctoral program’s emphasis in US Catholic experience. Directing the graduate programs in the Department of Theology and Religious Studies. Overseeing these programs in collaboration with the department’s graduate committee and other faculty charged with supporting the graduate programs. Advising MA students and first-year PhD students and contributing to graduate student formation (e.g. colloquies, professionalization seminars). Guiding appropriate curricular development, recruitment, marketing, and seeking grants when appropriate, for the graduate programs. Supporting assessment and accreditation processes, in collaboration with the department’s graduate committee. The Spearin Chair receives support for their work from a staff coordinator of graduate studies, an administrative assistant shared with four other endowed chairs in the areas related to Catholic traditions, and a graduate assistant assigned to work with them on projects of their choosing. The Spearin Chair oversees a budget that not only supports graduate theological education, but also provides travel support for the Spearin Chair. When the Spearin Chair seeks promotion to full professor, their administrative accomplishments may constitute a major element of their portfolio, alongside their teaching, research, and service. The Program The graduate theological programs include an MA with options to focus in pastoral ministry or theological studies, as well as a PhD in Theology with an emphasis in US Catholic experience. The University of Dayton has offered master’s degrees in theology and related fields since the 1960s and continues to do so, in service of both the church and the academy and in collaboration with other departments and divisions of the University, including the International Marian Research Institute, Campus Ministry, and the Center for Catholic Education. The doctoral program features a multidisciplinary approach to theology as located in diverse communities with attention to historical and cultural contexts. The doctoral program recently celebrated its 25th anniversary. Successful alumni from both the MA and PhD programs - Catholic and Protestant - serve as teachers and leaders in higher education, pastoral ministry, and beyond, including as endowed chairs, in administrative leadership positions, in diocesan offices, in positions in various ecclesial communities, and more. jobs.title: Clinical Teaching Faculty
jobs.description: Advertised Position Title: Clinical Teaching Faculty Job Description: Works in collaboration with program lecture faculty providing instruction in the laboratory and/or clinical setting. The clinical teaching faculty will work with students to provide opportunities to apply learned skills and achieve the stated objectives and outcomes of the nursing course in which the students are enrolled. Essential Functions: Provides instruction in the clinical setting 24 hours per week; uses 16 hours per week for job related duties including completion of all requirements related to instruction, meeting attendance, and office hours. Works closely with the course lecture faculty to maximize learning experiences for students and delivers the content appropriate for the clinical/laboratory sessions. When in the clinical setting, provides unit with the course syllabus during the first week and plans with the agency staff to provide maximum learning experiences for students. Considers clients’ needs when planning student-learning experiences. Completes all necessary documentation including anecdotal notes and evaluations of students’ performance by the stated deadlines. Provides all necessary documentation to the program, course lecture faculty, and students by the stated deadlines. Communicates, without delay, with course lecture faculty when concerns with students’ clinical/laboratory performance become apparent. Participates in end of semester course meetings with faculty and laboratory staff and provides input regarding the clinical and/or laboratory components of the course. Provides feedback regarding curriculum related to clinical and laboratory objectives. On duty days prior to and after the conclusion of classes each semester and when not planning for or concluding a clinical experience, or when not in clinical instructor orientations, may participate in the preparation and maintenance of the laboratory spaces/supplies. Performs other duties related to the laboratory and/or clinical components of the program or facilities (e.g., operates mannequins and participates in simulation role-playing and debriefing). Based on program need, CTFs may cover a lecture (theory) or laboratory course as part of their 40 hour per week requirement. Due to the scheduling of course sections, the 40 hour per week requirement may fluctuate and will be averaged over the semester. Total hours in lecture and/or lab should not exceed those of a typical 15/16 week lecture/lab course. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Knowledge of OBN Chapter 5 rules and regulations for Nursing Education Programs. Knowledge of National Accreditation standards. Good communication skills, interpersonal skills, up-to-date clinical knowledge in acute medical/surgical units. Ability to communicate effectively with students, faculty, and hospital staff. Ability to make decisions under pressure. Ability to manage several projects at one time. Ability to provide positive feedback to students. Ability to work with hospital staff, students, patients and family members. Professional attitude and presence. Professional demeanor under pressure. Strong level of commitment to the nursing profession and the nursing program. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor's degree Completion of an approved registered nursing education program. Experience of at least two years in the practice of nursing as a registered nurse. Current, valid, unencumbered license as a registered nurse in Ohio. Competence in the area of clinical practice in which the clinical teaching faculty is providing supervision to a student. Preferred: Master's degree Preferred clinical experience in medical/surgical nursing. Prior experience in clinical supervision of students, and evaluation procedures preferred. Ability to make decisions under pressure. Ability to manage several projects at one time. Ability to provide positive feedback to students. Job Title: Integrative Medicine, Endowed Chair, Functional Medicine Physician (Open Rank/Track Faculty) Department: The Ohio State University College of Medicine and Wexner Medical Center seek an exceptional Functional Medicine Physician to join our Center for Integrative Health, practice functional medicine, and lead the development of an innovative integrative primary care service line. The Center for Integrative Health’s vision for this new service line is to strengthen collaborations with specialties, including, but not limited to, Oncology, Long COVID, Women’s Health, Neurology, etc. This is a hybrid role combining clinical practice with strategic administrative responsibilities. The successful candidate will take a patient-centered, individualized, and science-based approach to address the root causes of chronic disease rather than managing isolated symptoms. This role combines 60% clinical practice with 40% strategic administrative responsibilities. Opportunity Overview The Center for Integrative Health at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center is a nationally recognized leader in evidence-based integrative medicine, dedicated to advancing whole-person care through clinical services, education, and research. As part of one of the nation’s largest academic health systems, the center brings together conventional medicine and complementary therapies to support optimal health and well-being across the lifespan. Our multidisciplinary team provides a comprehensive suite of integrative services, including acupuncture, chiropractic care, functional and lifestyle medicine, integrative nutrition, osteopathic manipulative treatment, mind-body medicine, massage therapy, and personalized wellness consultations. These services are grounded in scientific evidence and designed to work in partnership with traditional medical care to address the physical, emotional, and behavioral contributors to health. In addition to clinical care, the Center for Integrative Health plays a vital role in education and innovation. The program trains medical students, residents, fellows, and practicing clinicians in integrative health principles. It actively collaborates with campus and community partners to promote preventive care and research-driven wellness initiatives. Flagship programs, such as Mindfulness in Motion, reflect the Center’s commitment to developing scalable interventions that improve patient outcomes, reduce stress, and enhance overall resilience. With a mission rooted in holistic, patient-centered care, the Center for Integrative Health is advancing the future of integrative medicine in an academic environment—bringing together expert clinicians, researchers, educators, and innovators to transform how health and healing are delivered.
